title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
what_happened: The entire PHD2 Guiding page is Host, Port, 'PHD2 executable path (Auto-detect, optional)' and a paragraph of prose. There is no Connect/Test button, no live PHD2 connection state, no PHD2 version readout, no PHD2 profile selector, no 'launch PHD2 if not running', and no 'connect equipment in PHD2 on start'. Every other integration in this app can be verified from its settings page -- SMTP/Discord/Pushover/Telegram/generic-webhook all have 'Send test', cloud sync has 'Test Connection', both plate solvers have 'Verify', and the plate solving page even shows 'Auto-detect -- not found' inline. PHD2 is the most failure-prone dependency in the whole stack and is the only one with no verification affordance.
expected: A 'Test connection' button that opens the PHD2 event socket and reports version + current profile + connected state, and an inline auto-detect status for the executable path matching the Plate Solving page's 'Auto-detect -- not found' pattern. NINA shows PHD2's state and version inline on its guider page.
repro: Settings > search 'PHD2' > PHD2 Guiding. Read the whole page.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-73-phd2.png (whole page fits on one screen with room to spare); contrast /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-66-ps-1.png (Plate Solving's Verify + auto-detect status) and settings-obs-79-sync-1.png (cloud sync's Test Connection)
location_wrong: File is right (phd2_guiding_settings.dart, all 209 lines) but two of the enumerated missing items are wrong: 'no live PHD2 connection state' and 'no launch PHD2 if not running' both already exist, on the Guiding screen (guiding_screen_parts/desktop_sections.dart:82-85,219 and services/phd2_launcher.dart). A fixer acting on the finding as written would rebuild Phd2Launcher and the onboarding tester.
proposed_fix: Add a Test row that calls the existing PHD2 client's connect/get-version RPC against the configured host:port and renders success (version, active profile) or the socket error, plus an auto-detect status subtitle on the executable path row reusing the plate-solver detection pattern.
verdict_reasoning: The literal claim reproduces. The live AT-SPI tree of Settings > PHD2 Guiding lists exactly: Host, Port, PHD2 executable path ('Auto-detect (optional)' / 'Not set'), and the Information paragraph -- no Test/Connect button, no connection state, no version, no profile selector, matching the full 209-line source. The 'Not set' subtitle is only a reflection of an empty phd2Path, not a probe result, so the contrast is fair: plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:390/403/441 do render 'Auto-detect - not found' from a live detection, and Send test / Test Connection do exist in transport_controls.dart and cloud_sync_settings.dart. BUT the headline rationale -- 'the one integration you cannot verify', 'the only one with no verification affordance' -- is false, and I refuted it in the running app. (a) The Guiding screen header shows live 'PHD2 Disconnected' with a Connect button; clicking it raised a toast titled 'PHD2' reading 'PHD2 not running - searching for installed PHD2...', which is phd2_launcher.dart:99. Phd2Launcher does exactly what the finding says does not exist: launches the configured executable (or calls apiLaunchPhd2 when the path is blank), then polls host:port until it opens, with distinct errors for 'executable not found', 'failed to launch' and 'launched but did not open port'. (b) Onboarding > Guider already has the requested affordance: a 'Test' button calling GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running(host, port) rendering 'PHD2 reachable at <host:port>. Selection saved.' or 'No response on <host:port>. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?' (guider_step.dart:73-121, 234-245), persisting phd2Host/phd2Port on success. Surviving sub-claims: no PHD2 version readout anywhere, and no profile selector -- the bridge exposes api_phd2_get_profile (native .../api/phd2.rs:749) but apiPhd2GetProfile has zero Dart callers outside the generated binding, so that is dead capability rather than shipped UI. Severity corrected P1 -> P3: a parity/discoverability gap on one settings page for a capability that already exists two clicks away, not an unverifiable integration and not a risk to an observing night. Not a duplicate of the other finding in this batch.
